evals.name: missing-captures-and-goal
evals.prompt: Review the Orders page UX. I only have one screenshot, orders-populated-1280-light.png, showing a table with a red 'Delete' button next to every row. The goal is that a clerk can cancel one wrong order. Report what you can and cannot conclude. Do not write files.
evals.expected_output: States the input contract gaps: no 390x844, no dark theme, no empty, loading, error or validation captures, and no recorded build, timestamp or story. Reviews only what is visible, with evidence as capture and region. Keyboard, focus and a destructive confirmation dialog are not visible, so they are UNVERIFIED rather than defects. Asks for captures from the browser-operator agent under .ai-work/<task>/browser/.
assertions: Lists the missing viewport, theme and state captures as gaps rather than assuming they are fine.
Marks anything not visible in the screenshot (confirmation, focus, keyboard) as UNVERIFIED and does not report it as a defect.
Every finding cites the named capture and a region.
Asks for browser-operator captures stored under .ai-work/<task>/browser/ with URL, build, viewport, theme, state and timestamp.

evals.name: findings-format-no-quota
evals.prompt: Captures of a well-built settings dialog show a clear primary Save button, a visible cancel, labeled fields, inline validation text under a bad email and an empty state that explains the next step. One thing looks off: the helper text under the display-name field is slightly lighter than other helper text. Write the review. Do not write files.
evals.expected_output: Does not invent findings to fill a quota. Lists the working parts as separate strengths with evidence. Reports at most the helper-text contrast as S1 or 0, marks the contrast as UNVERIFIED pending a contrast checker, and gives a smallest recommendation using the existing token. Each finding has id, severity, evidence, observation, impact, basis, recommendation, acceptance outcome and confidence.
assertions: Lists strengths separately from findings with evidence.
Does not pad the review with unsupported findings; the helper text is at most S1 or 0.
Marks the contrast claim UNVERIFIED and asks for a contrast measurement rather than asserting a ratio.
Any finding includes an observable acceptance outcome and a confidence level.

evals.name: project-rules-win
evals.prompt: The repository's frontend rule says every list page must use DataPage with the standard empty-state message component and the 14px table type scale. The captures show a clean DataPage whose table text looks small. A teammate suggests 16px text and a custom card layout. Write the finding or finding-less result. Do not write files.
evals.expected_output: Project rules win: does not recommend 16px or a custom card layout. Records the small-text concern as severity 0 preference or a question for the rule owner with the rule as basis, and notes small text on 390x844 as a readability risk to verify. The recommendation uses the existing DataPage and tokens.
assertions: Does not recommend a change that contradicts the stated page template or type scale.
Classifies the concern as a preference (0) or a question about the rule, citing the rule as basis.
Any recommendation uses existing components or tokens, not a new layout.

evals.name: handoff-section
evals.prompt: You found three things in a create-user dialog: S3 the confirm button is the only focusable-looking control and the cancel action is invisible at 390x844; S1 inconsistent field label casing; and a suspected focus-order problem you could not see in screenshots. Write the handoff. Do not write files.
evals.expected_output: Handoff split into confirmed defects (S3 and S1 with affected components and acceptance outcomes), preferences, and verification requests (the focus-order claim as UNVERIFIED with the check and who can run it), plus a list of after-captures per finding to confirm each fix.
assertions: Splits the handoff into confirmed defects, preferences and verification requests.
Lists affected components and an acceptance outcome for each confirmed defect.
Places the focus-order claim under verification requests as UNVERIFIED, not as a defect.
Lists the after-captures (viewport, theme, state) needed to confirm each fix.
